evidence: M-O s.v. football: rugby: American football
terms.comment: Classically harpastum is a small hard ball and the rough game played with it, in which the players snatched the ball from one another (Mart. 4.19.6, 7.67.4).
Andresian’s name for the American game and its ball; Traupman keeps it for rugby (see rugby).
Traupman’s “football in the American way”, with a list of its terms (touchdown, quarterback).

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency: p. 47, checked against the searchable text of the book on 11 November 2026.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. football: rugby: American football.
